English: Stick Corral
A simple enclosure of sharpened sticks and thorn branches, quickly assembled to pen livestock for a nomadic camps first herds.
Wooden Pen
A more robust pen of timber and woven branches, improving herd safety and allowing greater livestock management.
Wattle Shelter
Wattle and daub shelters provide shade and basic protection for animals, increasing herd survival and supply.
Cattle Pavilion
Large pavilions of wood and thatch offer shelter for growing herds, and space for milking, birthing, and communal care.
Expanded Pen
Enlarged and fortified pens with separate areas for calves and adults, improving herd health and management. Requires advanced construction knowledge.
Guarded Yard
A large enclosure patrolled by herders and equipped with night fires and watch platforms, reducing livestock loss and increasing safety.
Village Pen
A communal pen at the center of the encampment, reinforced with clay and earthworks, supporting large livestock populations and reflecting growing clan organization.
Community Pavilion
A large, tented structure and festal space, the heart of the encampments livestock culture, boosting unity, trade, and celebration.
Chiefs Pen
A grand pen reserved for the clans most prized herds and symbolic animals, guarded and maintained by appointed elders. A mark of prestige and leadership.
West African Grand Pen
A sprawling, multi-chambered enclosure and festival ground, famed across the Sahel. Here, vast herds are cared for, deals are struck, and the clans greatness is displayed for all.
